arxiv-2301-07513.title: A Bayesian Nonparametric Stochastic Block Model for Directed Acyclic Graphs
arxiv-2301-07513.creator: Clement Lee, Marco Battiston
arxiv-2301-07513.description: Abstract Random graphs have been widely used in statistics, for example in network and social interaction analysis. In some applications, data may contain an inherent hierarchical ordering among its vertices, which prevents any directed edge between pairs of vertices that do not respect this order. For example, in bibliometrics, older papers cannot cite newer ones.

arxiv-2309-02936.creator: Hongyi Zhang 1 , Jan Bosch 1 , Helena Holmström Olsson 2
arxiv-2309-02936.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising approach for collaborative machine learning, addressing data privacy concerns. However, existing FL platforms and frameworks often present challenges for software engineers in terms of complexity, limited customization options, and scalability limitations.

arxiv-2309-09353.title: Many-body interactions between contracting living cells
arxiv-2309-09353.creator: Roman Golkov, Yair Shokef
arxiv-2309-09353.description: Abstract The organization of live cells into tissues and their subsequent biological function involves inter-cell mechanical interactions, which are mediated by their elastic environment. To model this interaction, we consider cells as spherical active force dipoles surrounded by an unbounded elastic matrix.

arxiv-2508-20816.title: Multi-Agent Penetration Testing AI for the Web
arxiv-2508-20816.creator: Isaac David, Arthur Gervais
arxiv-2508-20816.description: Abstract AI-powered development platforms are making software creation accessible to a broader audience, but this democratization has triggered a scalability crisis in security auditing. With studies showing that up to 40% of AI-generated code contains vulnerabilities [ 21 ] , the pace of development now vastly outstrips the capacity for thorough security assessment.

arxiv-2510-23281.title: New Hypernuclei Measurements from STAR
arxiv-2510-23281.creator: \firstname Yingjie \lastname Zhou \fnsep (For the STAR Collaboration)
arxiv-2510-23281.description: Abstract Hypernuclei are bound states of hyperons (Y) and nucleons (N). Measurements on their yields can help us investigate their production mechanisms. In particular, the Λ 5 {}^{5}_{\Lambda} He and Λ 4 {}^{4}_{\Lambda} H(e) are bounded substantially tighter compared to the Λ 3 {}^{3}_{\Lambda} H.

arxiv-2510-25135.title: Conditional neural field for spatial dimension reduction of turbulence data: a comparison study Journal: Elsevier
arxiv-2510-25135.creator: Junyi Guo, Pan Du, Xiantao Fan, Yahui Li, Jian-Xun Wang
arxiv-2510-25135.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Junyi Guo, Pan Du, Xiantao Fan, Yahui Li, Jian-Xun Wang. We investigate conditional neural fields (CNFs), mesh-agnostic, coordinate-based decoders conditioned on a low-dimensional latent, for spatial dimensionality reduction of turbulent flows. CNFs are benchmarked against Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and a convolutional autoencoder within a unified encoding–decoding framework and a common evaluation protocol that explicitly separates in-range (interpolative) from out-of-range (strict extrapolative) testing beyond the training horizon, with identical preprocessing, metrics, and fixed splits across all baselines.
